chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a village belonging to some people of the Dhimmah (non-Muslims under protection), I do not know if its original ownership belongs to them or not, except that it is in their hands and they pay the land tax (kharaj). The ruler encroached upon them, so they came to me, and they gave me their land and village on the condition that I would suffice them against the ruler, whether the cost was little or much. After the ruler took what he took, there remained a surplus for me. He said: 'There is no harm in that; whatever surplus remained is yours.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the Covenant (non-Muslims living under Islamic rule)

ai.seo_question: Is the surplus profit from buying land tax rights from Dhimmis lawful if the original ownership is uncertain?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* under the chapter of *Muzara'ah*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the permissibility of acquiring property through a 'kafah' contract, where one pays the ruler's dues on behalf of Ahl al-Dhimmah to secure their land. The Imam’s ruling that the surplus belongs to the payer highlights the practical application of private initiative in public finance during the era of the Imams, affirming the validity of such transactions even when original ownership was ambiguous. This serves as a foundational precedent for Islamic jurisprudence regarding tax farming and property acquisition through contractual defense of rights.
